was: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on Little Piney Creek (trout stream) near Rolla; 17 sites (6 electric, 11 basic) with 6 creekside, RVs to ~34 ft; sites are FCFS (only the group pavilion is reservable); open Apr-Oct. --Claude

was: USFS Mark Twain NF campground nestled along Paddy Creek near Licking; 19 non-electric sites (asphalt pads to ~34 ft), no potable water; FCFS via fee tube; open Apr-Dec. --Claude

was: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on Marble Creek near Fredericktown (Ozark Trail trailhead); 26 non-electric sites, 6 directly creekside, no potable water; FCFS via fee tube; open Apr-Oct. --Claude

was: USFS Mark Twain NF campground ~150 ft from the Current River near Doniphan; some 30/50A electric and many non-electric sites (RVs to 40 ft) with pressurized water; individual sites are FCFS; open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

was: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on the Black River near Ellsinore; a 50A electric loop (Birch) plus three non-electric loops, with showers and drinking water; reservable online May-Labor Day, FCFS otherwise; open May-Oct. --Claude

was: Developed USFS Mark Twain NF campground for the Chadwick motorized-trail area near Chadwick; 45 sites incl. ~25 electric (30/50A), paved pads to 45 ft with showers; standard sites reservable online plus some FCFS; open year-round (no horses). --Claude

was: FCFS primitive lakeside camping at Hunnewell Lake (MDC) with drive-through sites, vault toilets and a dump station behind the ranger station; no hookups. --Claude
note: Primitive lakeside camping at Hunnewell Lake (MDC) with a dump station behind the ranger station. --Claude

was: FCFS primitive camping (MDC) in level gravel lots beside Big Lake near Williamsburg; drive-in off a maintained gravel road, vault toilets, no hookups. --Claude

was: FCFS primitive camping (MDC) at several drive-in campgrounds off gravel roads near Lewistown, including a Lake Campground on Deer Ridge Lake; privies, no hookups. --Claude

was: FCFS camping (MDC) at a ~50-site gravel main campground (about 26 sites fit trailers) with a privy, near the Niangua River and Jakes Creek; drive-in, no hookups. --Claude
note: Camping (MDC) at a gravel main campground (about 26 sites fit trailers) near the Niangua River and Jakes Creek; drive-in. --Claude

was: City of Brookfield park with ~10 FCFS pull-through sites (30/50A electric and water) and a dump station via on-site fee box; front sites are more level for a 23-ft rig. --Claude
note: City of Brookfield park; on-site fee box; front sites are more level for a 23-ft rig. --Claude

was: City of Shelbina park on Shelbina Lake with ~90 FCFS electric sites (mostly 30/50A) paid at the golf pro shop or City Hall; open late Mar-Oct. --Claude
note: City of Shelbina park on Shelbina Lake with electric sites (mostly 30/50A) paid at the golf pro shop or City Hall. --Claude

was: 109-acre KDWP state fishing lake in the Flint Hills west of Cottonwood Falls; primitive camping, first come first served, on about a dozen gravel spurs along the north shore, eight or nine of which suit an RV (camper report, April 2026). Vault toilets, no hookups. --Claude

was: KDWP state fishing lake (40-acre lake, 225-acre wildlife area) 5 mi S and 2.5 mi E of Ness City. Primitive camping beside the gravel parking areas above the lake's west shore, with picnic shelters, a vault toilet, a boat ramp and a courtesy dock. Roads are dirt and rut when wet (1/2026 camper). FCFS, 7 nights at most. --Claude
note: KDWP state fishing lake (40-acre lake, 225-acre wildlife area) 5 mi S and 2.5 mi E of Ness City. Primitive camping beside the gravel parking areas above the lake's west shore, with picnic shelters, a boat ramp and a courtesy dock. Roads are dirt and rut when wet (1/2026 camper). --Claude

was: Sedgwick County park, 720 acres around the 258-acre Lake Afton, W of Wichita. RV camping in several areas around the shore (Fisherman's Cove by the observatory, Shelter #5 on Fellowship Cove, Cottonwood Grove), with electric at many sites, water at 16, a dump station and restrooms (three open in winter). No generators. Permits at the park office or kiosk, no reservations; 14 days, then 5 days away, 56 days a year at most. Blue-green algae warnings in summer (call 316-660-1780). --Claude

was: City of Parsons lake NW of Parsons in Labette County, reached by about 2 mi of unpaved road: an improved campsite area of concrete-slab sites with electric and water on a wooded peninsula, with boat ramp and docks, playground, bath house and a summer camp host; free primitive camping where there is no pad. Permits from the City Clerk ($300 a year), no reservations, 12-day limit. --Claude

was: 25 non-electric sites on a point in Lake Granby (Arapaho NRA), elev ~8,300 ft; max vehicle length 46 ft, sites 12-24 are the longer ones. Potable water but no threaded spigots, vault toilets, trash service, boat ramp; no hookups. First-come, first-served (not reservable on recreation.gov). --Claude
note: Sites on a point in Lake Granby (Arapaho NRA), elev ~8,300 ft; sites 12-24 are the longer ones. Potable water but no threaded spigots, trash service, boat ramp. --Claude

was: Platte River WMA adjacent to I-80 SE of Kearney. Drive-in primitive camping: flat pull-offs along a gravel road, self-contained rigs fit, no facilities and no fires; no permit, FCFS, 3-night limit per 6 days. Riverside fishing access. Note: access bridge has weight limits (10-ton dual-axle / 23-ton trailer) — fine for a 23-ft Class C. Highway noise. --Claude

was: Nebraska Game & Parks WMA on Big Alkali Lake in the Sandhills, ~25 mi south of Valentine via US-83 and Spur 16B (well-maintained but narrow gravel). About 30 FCFS sites (no reservations); some have electric. Reviewers note leveled gravel big-rig-friendly sites to the right of the boat ramp plus a sandy dispersed area to the left. Vault toilets, picnic tables/grills, water spout/laundry house near entrance, boat ramp; no dump station. As a WMA this is drive-in vehicle camping (not walk-in/hunt-only). --Claude

was: NGPC state recreation area west of Bridgeport on five clear sandpit lakes (78 water acres) along the North Platte. 72 designated Basic camp sites plus ~130 non-designated primitive sites, all first-come first-served (no electric). RV dump/fill station near the entrance (open ~Apr 30-Oct 1); vault toilets, drinking water at the swim beach. Nebraska park entry permit required. --Claude

was: Largest campground at Calamus Reservoir SRA, 6 mi NW of Burwell in the Sandhills: paved, level 50-amp back-in sites with mature shade; shower house, modern restrooms, water; dump station and laundry in the park. The white-sand swimming beach and boat ramp are a separate day-use area to the southwest. Some sites reservable up to 180 days out, the rest FCFS. Park entry permit required. --Claude

was: NGPC recreation area on a Logan Creek/Elkhorn oxbow off US 275, ~4 mi north of Scribner, beside Powder Horn WMA. 17 electric sites (30 A) in a loop at the south end of the oxbow; the four primitive sites have been closed by flood damage. First-come first-served, self-pay envelopes. Drinking water, primitive restrooms; no dump station. --Claude

was: NGPC recreation area on Gallagher Canyon Reservoir, an irrigation lake whose level can drop in late summer, SE of Cozad (Dr. 752 off Rd 422). About 30 primitive sites without electricity on dirt tracks across the wooded peninsula west of the dam; first-come first-served year-round. Primitive restrooms; no drinking water, showers or dump station. --Claude

was: Village of Bancroft municipal park on the village's SW/NW edge; ~5 drive-in electric+water sites (camping NW of the park off Public Rd) on open flat grass -- ample room for a 23-ft Class C. RV dump and flush toilets on site; no showers noted. Open May-Oct, roughly $6/night, very cheap. Not on recreation.gov -- book/inquire by phone via Ru-Des Mini Mart; effectively FCFS/call-ahead. RV Life unrated (0 star, price $). --Claude

was: City-run 55-acre municipal park & arboretum (ball fields, pool, playground) on the south edge of Battle Creek. ~18 RV sites with electric (20/30/50 amp) and water; sanitary dump on site. FCFS, pay on site. No water feature at the park (Battle Creek/Elkhorn River not adjacent). Caveat (2026-11-05): the city's parks page doesn't mention camping and one trail guide lists only two campsites, so call City Hall (402-675-2165) before counting on a site. --Claude

was: City of Bloomfield municipal park. 6 RV-only sites (no tents) with cement pads, full hookups (30-amp electric + water), fire pits, grills, picnic tables; flush toilets, swimming pool/playground in park. Open year-round. FCFS, pay at City Office or police drop box. RV Life unrated (0 stars). --Claude

was: City of Seward municipal campground at 730 S 6th St. 16 crushed-rock pads with 30-amp electric; pads fit large rigs (reviewer at 34 ft). Dump station, water hydrant, portable ADA restroom (no showers), playground. $15 senior 65+, $10 tent, FCFS via drop-box envelopes, open Apr 1-Nov 1, 7-day stay limit (48-hr interim). Sits in a city park west of the Big Blue River, not on the water. --Claude

was: Village of Cody municipal park; small grassy camping area near the old grain elevator (shields US-20 noise), behind the C-store a block off the highway. Directory reports (Campendium, Allstays, a 2023 blog): ~4-10 unmarked full-hookup back-in sites (30/50 A, water, sewer) beside pedestals, dump station, max RV ~29 ft, restrooms not always open, $20 a night honor system (cash/check), FCFS, open ~May 1-Oct 15. The village has no website (the old villageofcody.com domain now forwards to an unrelated site); call the village clerk. --Claude
